mainTopic: Oil for the מנורה and מנחות, the מנורה as a testimony of the שכינה, and choosing wine for נסכים
overview: The גמרא first asks how the משנה can call two grades of oil 'equal' when only the first grade of each harvest is fit for the מנורה. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that they are equal only for מנחות. A ברייתא then defines זך and כתית and proves from a פסוק that this top oil is also fit for מנחות. The Torah required it only for the מנורה, because it cares about the money of the Jewish people. Next comes a series of aggadic teachings: the oil is 'for you', the שולחן and מנורה stand apart, and the windows of the בית המקדש were narrow inside and wide outside. All of these show that הקב״ה does not need food or light. Instead, the light of the מנורה is a testimony that the שכינה rests in ישראל, shown by the miracle of the נר מערבי. A new משנה then ranks wine for נסכים: the best regions, wines not chosen at first but valid if brought, and wines that are פסול even if brought. It ends with rules for storing the wine and pouring it from the cask, and that last rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can the two grades be called equal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's claim that two grades of oil are equal, since the משנה also said that only the first grade is fit for the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Equal? But you said the first grade is for the מנורה and the rest are for מנחות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks a line in the משנה that calls the second oil of the first harvest and the first oil of the second harvest 'equal.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also said that the first oil of every harvest goes to the מנורה. That means the first oil of the second harvest is good enough for the מנורה, but the second oil of the first harvest is not. So how can the two be equal?

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't you say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Equal?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה's word 'equal,' used for the second oil of the first harvest and the first oil of the second harvest.

phrases.english: But didn't you say
the first is for the Candelabrum
and the rest are for meal offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the two grades are 'equal'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one of the two grades is fit for the מנורה, so they cannot be fully equal.

steps.title: They are equal only for meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'equal' means equal for use in מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'equal' mean? Equal for meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question by narrowing what the משנה meant by 'equal.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never said the two grades are equal in every way. For the מנורה, the first oil really is better. But for מנחות, where both are allowed, neither one is preferred over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: equal with regard to meal offerings

steps.whatToRemember: 'Equal' in the משנה means equal for מנחות, not for the מנורה.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
What does 'equal' mean?
Equal for meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Equal' seemed to mean equal in every way.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Equal' means equal only for use in מנחות.

steps.title: What 'refined' and 'pounded' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and then brings a ברייתא that defines זך and כתית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Also all the meal offerings should logically need this oil, etc.' The Rabbis taught: 'זך' means only clean oil. רבי יהודה says: 'כתית' means only crushed olives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It brings a ברייתא defining the two words of the פסוק about the מנורה oil, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires oil that is 'זך כתית.' The ברייתא explains that זך means clean, pure oil, and רבי יהודה explains that כתית means olives that were crushed. This tells us what the top-quality oil is before asking whether it may be used for מנחות.

phrases.english: Also [all] the meal offerings
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. Some versions add the words in square brackets; וכו׳ means 'etc.,' pointing to the rest of the line.

phrases.english: it was logical [etc.].
The Rabbis taught: 'Refined' —
'refined' means nothing but clean;
Rabbi Yehuda says: 'Pounded' —
'pounded' means nothing but crushed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זך means clean oil; כתית means crushed olives.

steps.title: A פסוק shows pounded oil is fine for meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that זך כתית oil might be unfit for מנחות, and proves from a פסוק that it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think refined, pounded oil is unfit for meal offerings. So the פסוק says: 'And a tenth of fine flour mixed with pounded oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake and corrects it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah says this oil is 'for lighting,' one might think it is only for the מנורה and is forbidden for מנחות. But the פסוק about the מנחה of the daily offering mentions 'שמן כתית,' which shows it may be used for מנחות too.

keyTerms.meaning: a tenth (of an איפה), a measure of flour

phrases.english: One might think that refined, pounded oil
is unfit for meal offerings?
Therefore the verse says:
'And a tenth of fine flour'
mixed with pounded oil.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא זָךְ כָּתִית פָּסוּל לִמְנָחוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definitions to ask whether this oil is allowed for מנחות
steps.raayaObject: זך כתית oil is fit for מנחות

steps.title: Then why does the Torah say 'for lighting'?
steps.stepSummary: If the oil is fit for מנחות, the ברייתא asks what the word 'למאור' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'for lighting'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question. If the best oil is allowed for מנחות, the word 'for lighting' seems to teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זך כתית למאור' seemed to limit this oil to the מנורה. Now that we know it is fit for מנחות, the ברייתא needs a new reason for the word 'למאור.'

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say
'for lighting'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of the פסוק in light of the proof in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oil is fit for מנחות, the limiting word 'for lighting' seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The requirement is only for the מנורה, to save money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that 'למאור' means the finest oil is required only for the מנורה, to save money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of sparing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the word 'for lighting': the finest oil is required only for the מנורה, not for מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'למאור' does not forbid this oil for מנחות. It means only the מנורה must use it, so that people do not have to buy expensive top-grade oil for every מנחה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'למאור' does not mean the best oil is forbidden for מנחות. It means it is required only for the מנורה; for מנחות it is allowed but not needed.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of sparing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'למאור' seemed to limit this oil to the מנורה alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'למאור' means it is required only for the מנורה, to save money for מנחות.

steps.title: What does 'sparing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'חיסכון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'sparing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the word 'sparing,' which sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used a short, unclear word. The גמרא wants to know whose money is being saved and why.

phrases.english: What is 'sparing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the key word in step 6

steps.title: The Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the Torah spared Jewish people's money by not requiring the expensive oil for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that the Torah wanted to save the Jewish people money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Top-grade oil is expensive, and there are many מנחות. By requiring it only for the מנורה, the Torah spared people a heavy cost.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah has pity, cares about
the money of the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: The finest oil (זך כתית) is required only for the מנורה. It is allowed for מנחות but not required, because the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous principle: 'התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל.' The Torah takes the cost to the Jewish people into account.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Torah has pity
on the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah spared the money of the Jewish people by not requiring expensive oil for מנחות.

steps.title: The oil is 'for you,' because God does not need light
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads the word 'אליך' in the פסוק about the oil for the מנורה as teaching that the light is for ישראל, not for הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Command the children of Israel, and they shall take for yourself pure olive oil.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: 'For yourself' and not for Me. I do not need light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the oil for the מנורה, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains one word in it: 'אליך,' 'for you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have just said 'take olive oil.' The extra word 'אליך' tells us whose benefit the light is for: ישראל, not הקב״ה. This opens a new theme: the מנורה is not there because הקב״ה needs light.

keyTerms.meaning: To you / for you. The word the דרשה is built on.
Pure olive oil, the oil used for the מנורה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme for the next few steps: every detail of the מנורה and the בית המקדש shows that הקב״ה has no need of it.

phrases.english: "Command the children of Israel,
and they shall take for yourself pure olive oil"
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says:
"For yourself" and not for Me,
I do not need light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic topic of oil quality (steps 4-8) to a new aggadic theme about the purpose of the מנורה, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'אליך' teaches that the light of the מנורה is for ישראל, since הקב״ה does not need light.

steps.title: The שולחן and מנורה stand apart, because הקב״ה does not need food or light
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא in the name of רבי אלעזר shows from the placement of the שולחן in the north and the מנורה in the south that הקב״ה needs neither food nor light.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שולחן is in the north and the מנורה is in the south. רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: I do not need it for eating, and I do not need it for light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching on the same theme, this time from where the שולחן and the מנורה stood in the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who eats puts the lamp right next to his table. In the היכל, the שולחן and מנורה were on opposite sides of the room. This shows the bread is not a 'meal' for הקב״ה and the light is not 'for Him' either.

keyTerms.meaning: The Table that held the לחם הפנים (showbread).

phrases.english: The Table is in the north,
and the Menorah is in the south.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika says that Rabbi Elazar says:
I do not need it for eating,
and I do not need it for light.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא לַאֲכִילָה אֲנִי צָרִיךְ, וְלֹא לְאוֹרָה אֲנִי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source for the idea in step 9, and widens it to include food (the שולחן) as well as light.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The separate placement of the שולחן and מנורה shows that הקב״ה needs neither food nor light.

steps.title: The Temple windows were narrow inside and wide outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the windows of שלמה's בית המקדש: they were built backwards from normal windows, showing that the light was meant to go out, not come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he made for the House windows שקופים אטומים.' A ברייתא taught: narrow on the inside and wide on the outside. I do not need light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof for the same idea, from the shape of the windows in the בית המקדש that שלמה built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal windows are wide on the inside so outside light spreads into the room. These windows were the reverse, narrow inside and wide outside. So the בית המקדש did not need light from outside; its light went out to the world.

keyTerms.meaning: The windows described in the פסוק, explained here as narrow-inside, wide-outside.

phrases.english: "And he made for the House windows narrow and broad"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:4, about the בית המקדש that שלמה built.

phrases.english: A ברייתא taught: narrow on the inside,
and wide on the outside,
I do not need light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source for the same theme, moving from the כלים inside the היכל to the building itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The windows of the בית המקדש were narrow inside and wide outside, showing that הקב״ה does not need light.

steps.title: The מנורה's light is a testimony that the שכינה rests in ישראל
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'פרוכת העדות,' the גמרא explains what the light is really for: it testifies to the whole world that the שכינה rests among ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Outside the Curtain of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting.' It is a testimony to everyone in the world that the שכינה rests among ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: After showing what the light is NOT for, the גמרא now explains what it IS for, using the word 'העדות' in the פסוק about lighting the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curtain is called the 'Curtain of the Testimony.' The light of the מנורה, lit right next to it, is a testimony that the שכינה dwells among ישראל. So the light is not a need of הקב״ה but a sign to the world.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain separating the קודש from the קודש הקדשים.
Testimony, a sign that proves something.
The Tent of Meeting, the משכן.
Literally 'those who come into the world': all people.

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches one idea: the מנורה, the שולחן and the windows of the בית המקדש are not for הקב״ה's needs. The light is for ישראל and serves as a sign to the world that the שכינה rests among them.

phrases.english: "Outside the Curtain of the Testimony
in the Tent of Meeting"
It is a testimony to all of humanity
that the Divine Presence rests among Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After three teachings saying what the light is not for, this gives its positive purpose. The next step defends it, and steps 14-15 explain what the testimony actually was.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The light of the מנורה is a testimony to the world that the שכינה rests among ישראל.

steps.title: God does not need light, since He lit the way in the desert
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה proves that הקב״ה does not need the מנורה's light. ישראל walked forty years in the מדבר by His light. So the light must be a testimony that the שכינה rests in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the מנורה is lit because הקב״ה needs light, that cannot be. For all forty years ישראל walked in the desert, they walked only by His light. So the light must be a sign to the whole world that the שכינה rests among ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away a possible objection: maybe the מנורה really is there to give light. It proves from the desert years that הקב״ה gives light and does not need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could think the light is meant for הקב״ה's use. The answer is that He provided light for all of ישראל for forty years, so He obviously needs none. Once that option is gone, the only explanation left is that the light is a testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you say (introduces a possible objection)
but isn't it so? (introduces the rebuttal)
forty years (the years in the מדבר)

steps.whatToRemember: The light of the מנורה is not for הקב״ה. It is a testimony to the whole world that the שכינה rests in ישראל.

phrases.english: And if you say: Do I need its light?
phrases.notes: This is said as if from הקב״ה's point of view: 'Do you think I need this light?'

phrases.english: But isn't it so that all forty years
that ישראל walked in the desert
they walked only by His light!
phrases.notes: His light means the pillar of fire that led them at night.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֵדוּת הוּא לְכׇל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם
phrases.english: Rather, it is testimony to all who come into the world
that the שכינה rests among ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: לְאוֹרָה אֲנִי צָרִיךְ? וַהֲלֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the דרשה on 'פרוכת העדות' by rejecting the idea that the light is for הקב״ה.
steps.raayaObject: That the מנורה's light is a testimony, not something הקב״ה needs
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישראל walked by His light for forty years in the מדבר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The light is testimony that the שכינה rests in ישראל.

steps.title: What exactly was the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the מנורה actually showed that the שכינה rests in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was its testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up רבא's answer. If the light is a testimony, what about it proved anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary lamps burning do not prove anything by themselves. So the גמרא wants to know what was special or miraculous that made the light a real testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: its testimony (the proof the מנורה gives)

phrases.english: What is its testimony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete meaning of the 'testimony' just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What about the מנורה served as proof of the שכינה

steps.title: The western lamp lasted longer than the others
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the testimony was the נר מערבי. It got the same oil as the other lamps, yet it kept burning long enough to light the others from it and to finish with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is the western lamp. They put the same amount of oil in it as in the others. From it the כהן would light the others, and with it he would finish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The miracle was the נר מערבי, which kept burning longer than it naturally should have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נר מערבי got exactly as much oil as the other lamps. Even so, it was still burning when the כהן came to light the מנורה, so he lit the others from it. He also prepared it last. That steady miracle was the visible sign of the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: the western lamp of the מנורה

steps.whatToRemember: The נר מערבי burned longer than the others on the same amount of oil. This was the constant miracle that showed the שכינה rests in ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that it got more oil. It got the SAME oil and still burned longer. That is what made it a miracle.

phrases.english: רבא said: This is the western lamp,
in which they put oil equal to its fellow lamps,
and from it he would light,
phrases.notes: It was still burning at lighting time, so the כהן lit the others from it.

phrases.english: and with it he would finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the testimony was.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The miraculous long burning of the נר מערבי
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The נר מערבי's miracle is the testimony of the שכינה.

steps.title: Where the wine for libations came from
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the best places for wine for נסכים: קדוחים and עטולין first, then בית רימה, בית לבן and כפר סיגנא. All places were valid, but they brought wine from these.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they bring the wine? קדוחים and עטולין are first-rate for wine. Second to them are בית רימה and בית לבן in the mountain, and כפר סיגנא in the valley. All lands were valid, but they brought it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, now about wine for נסכים. It names the places that had the best wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the earlier משנה ranked places for oil, this one ranks places for wine. It makes clear that wine from anywhere was valid. These places were simply the best choices.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think wine from other places is פסול. The משנה says outright that all lands were valid. These were just the best.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מֵאַיִן הָיוּ מְבִיאִין אֶת הַיַּיִן?
phrases.english: MISHNAH: From where would they bring the wine?
קדוחים and עטולין are first-rate for wine,
phrases.notes: אלפא is literally 'alpha,' the first letter, meaning number one.

phrases.english: second to them are
בית רימה and בית לבן in the mountain,
and כפר סיגנא in the valley.
All lands were valid,
but from here they would bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on wine, after the long discussion of oil and the מנורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine was brought from the best regions, though wine from any land is valid.

steps.title: Wines not brought at first but valid if brought
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says not to bring wine from fertilized vineyards, irrigated vineyards, or vineyards with grain sown between the vines. It also says not to bring הליסטיון. In all these cases the wine is still valid if brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring wine from a fertilized field, from an irrigated field, or from vines with seeds sown between them. If one brought it, it is valid. They do not bring הליסטיון. If one brought it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists wines that are not the first choice. If someone used them anyway, the נסכים still count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These wines are lower quality, so they should not be chosen at the start. They are not disqualified, though. Each list ends with 'if he brought it, it is valid.'

keyTerms.meaning: sweet wine made from sun-dried grapes
if he brought it, it is valid (after the fact)

phrases.english: They do not bring from a fertilized field,
nor from an irrigated field,
nor from what was sown between them,
phrases.notes: Between them means between the vines.

phrases.english: but if he brought it, it is valid.
They do not bring הליסטיון,
but if he brought it, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the best places to lower-quality wines that are still valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine from fertilized, irrigated, or sown-between vineyards, and הליסטיון, should not be brought at first, but is valid if brought.

steps.title: Argument about aged wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי says not to bring aged wine. The חכמים say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring old wine. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים rule it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about wine that has aged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that aged wine should not be used for נסכים. The חכמים disagree and allow it, so for them aged wine is fine.

phrases.english: They do not bring old wine; these are the words of רבי,
and the חכמים rule it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of wine, this time with a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: aged wine is not brought. חכמים: it is valid.

steps.title: Wines that are invalid even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: Sweet, smoked, and cooked wine may not be brought. If one brought it, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring sweet wine, smoked wine, or cooked wine. If one brought it, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists wines that are worse. These are disqualified even if someone already used them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list differs from step 17. There the ending was 'כשר,' valid after the fact. Here the ending is 'פסול,' invalid even after the fact.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the ending. Earlier lists ended 'כשר,' valid after the fact. This list ends 'פסול,' invalid even if brought.

phrases.english: They do not bring sweet wine,
nor smoked, nor cooked,
and if he brought it, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 17: these wines are invalid even after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweet, smoked, and cooked wine are פסול even if brought.

steps.title: Preferred grapes: low on the ground, from tended vineyards
steps.stepSummary: Wine is not brought from grapes hanging high on stakes or trees. It is brought from grapes growing low near the ground and from well-tended vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring wine from grapes hanging up high. They bring it from grapes growing low, and from vineyards that are worked.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying which grapes and vineyards are preferred for נסכים wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes that grow low and vineyards that are properly worked give better wine. This is about choosing the best wine, not about disqualifying anything.

keyTerms.meaning: vines hanging up high on stakes or trees
vines growing low, near the ground
vineyards that are worked and tended

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ranks wine for נסכים in three levels: the best wine to choose, wine that should not be chosen but is valid if brought, and wine that is פסול even if brought.

phrases.english: And they do not bring from hanging vines,
but from low-growing vines,
and from vineyards that are worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with which grapes and vineyards are preferred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine should come from low-growing vines and well-tended vineyards, not from hanging vines.

steps.title: Storing the wine in small casks that are not filled to the top
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says wine for נסכים is stored in small casks, not large barrels. The cask is not filled to the top, so the wine's smell can spread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wine is not gathered into large barrels, only into small casks. The cask is not filled all the way up to its mouth, so that the wine's fragrance can spread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is still listing how to prepare the best wine for נסכים. Now it moves from where the grapes grow to how the wine is stored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two storage rules. First, use small casks (חביות) and not large barrels (חצבין). Second, leave the cask partly empty, and the משנה itself gives the reason: so that the wine's smell will spread.

phrases.english: And one does not collect it into large barrels,
phrases.notes: "It" is the wine for נסכים that the משנה has been talking about.

phrases.english: rather, into small casks,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא אֶת הֶחָבִית עַד פִּיהָ,
phrases.english: and one does not fill the cask up to its mouth,
so that its fragrance will spread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of best practices for נסכים wine, moving from vineyard quality to storage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine for נסכים is stored in small casks, not large barrels, and the cask is left partly empty so the smell can spread.

steps.title: Not taking the wine from the top of the cask
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new rule: wine for נסכים is not taken from the mouth (top) of the cask. It begins giving a reason, which continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not bring wine from the mouth of the cask, because of...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins a new rule about which part of the cask's wine may be used. The sentence is cut off here, and the reason comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining how to store the wine, the משנה now tells us which wine to pour out of the cask. Wine from the very top is not used. The word מפני shows a reason is coming, but we have to wait for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From its mouth (the top opening of the cask)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't guess the reason yet. The sentence stops here, and the משנה gives its own reason in the very next words.

phrases.english: One does not bring from its mouth, because of
phrases.notes: "Its mouth" means the top of the cask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the cask storage described in step 21 by stating which part of the cask's wine is not used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine for נסכים is not taken from the top of the cask. The reason is given in the continuation.
